sections.overview: Apistogramma resticulosa is a small freshwater cichlid described by Sven Kullander in 1980 from the Rio Madeira system near Humaitá, Brazil.
sections.identification: FishBase lists a maximum standard length of 3.9 cm for male or unsexed fish. The name resticulosa refers to fine, thread-like markings on the abdomen. No reliable female maximum, mass, width or body-height value was found.
sections.habitat: The known range is the Madeira drainage near Humaitá, with a type locality at Igarapé Xicanga about 5 km west of the town.
sections.diet: No species-specific diet study was located. A specialist account infers that it picks small invertebrates from leaf litter and sediment, but this has not been confirmed by stomach-content samples for A. resticulosa.
sections.behavior: FishBase notes a modest sex difference: males have pointed fins, whereas females have rounded fins.
sections.reproduction: Eggs are attached to a cave ceiling and cared for by the female; the species summary gives no reliable clutch-size range.
sections.ecology: Kullander placed the species in the Apistogramma regani group. Compared with A. regani, it has short diagonal abdominal dashes rather than full stripes; both have a striped tail, so the belly pattern is the clearer clue.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern for the species, assessed on 29 October 2020.
